1.o: The scope and design of this chapter is to confirm our faith in Christ as the eternal Son of God, and the true Messiah and Saviour of the world, that we may be brought to receive him, and rely upon him, as our Prophet, Priest, and King, and to give up ourselves to be ruled, and taught, and saved by him. In order to this, we have here, I. An account given of him by the inspired penman himself, fairly laying down, in the beginning, what he designed his whole book should be the proof of (ver. 1-5); and again (ver.

2.o: In the close of the foregoing chapter we had an account of the first disciples whom Jesus called, Andrew and Peter, Philip and Nathanael. These were the first-fruits to God and to the Lamb, Rev. xiv. 4. Now, in this chapter, we have, I. The account of the first miracle which Jesus wrought-turning water into wine, at Cana of Galilee (ver. 1-11), and his appearing at Capernaum, ver. 12. II.
2.i: At a wedding in Cana, Jesus turns water into wine and shows his glory for the first time.
2.p: Lord Jesus, You bring joy and fill our empty jars. Thank You for Your care in small things. Amen.
2.l: Help someone enjoy a celebration this week, by bringing something, setting the table, or cleaning up.
q: Jesus cared about a family's embarrassment at a party. What small need might He be asking you to notice?

3.o: In this chapter we have, I. Christ's discourse with Nicodemus, a Pharisee, concerning the great mysteries of the gospel, in which he here privately instructs him, ver. 1-21. II. John Baptist's discourse with his disciples concerning Christ, upon occasion of his coming into the neighbourhood where John was (ver. 22-36), in which he fairly and faithfully resigns all his honour and interest to him.
3.i: The Pharisee Nicodemus visits Jesus by night and hears about being born again and God's love for the world.
3.p: Lord Jesus, You came to save the world. Give us new birth by Your Spirit, and the courage to follow You. Amen.
3.l: Ask Jesus a question today, even a hard one, and listen for an answer.
q: Nicodemus came at night and later spoke up for Jesus. How can you move from a quiet question to a public stand?

4.o: It was, more than any thing else, the glory of the land of Israel, that it was Emmanuel's land (Isa. viii. 8), not only the place of his birth, but the scene of his preaching and miracles. This land in our Saviour's time was divided into three parts: Judea in the south, Galilee in the north, and Samaria lying between them. Now, in this chapter, we have Christ in each of these three parts of that land. I. Departing out of Judea, ver. 1-3. II.
4.i: Jesus talks with a Samaritan woman at Jacob's well, tells her He is the Messiah, and her whole town comes to hear Him.
4.p: Lord Jesus, You give living water. Satisfy our thirst, and send us to tell others. Amen.
4.l: Talk kindly to someone today who is different from you, and listen to their story.
q: Jesus broke the rules to talk with this woman. Who might He be asking you to talk with?

5.o: We have in the gospels a faithful record of all that Jesus began both to do and to teach, Acts i. 1. These two are interwoven, because what he taught explained what he did, and what he did confirmed what he taught. Accordingly, we have in this chapter a miracle and a sermon. I. The miracle was the cure of an impotent man that had been diseased thirty-eight years, with the circumstances of that cure, ver. 1-16. II.
5.s: Do You Want to Get Well?
5.i: A man paralyzed for thirty-eight years waited beside a healing pool, and Jesus healed him with a word, without any need for the water.
5.p: Lord Jesus, You are better than any pool. Heal what is broken in us, and help us to help those who are stuck. Amen.
5.l: Ask someone who seems stuck or alone what they need, then do one small thing to help.
q: Jesus asked the man if he wanted to be well. What do you want Jesus to do for you?

6.o: In this chapter we have, I. The miracle of the loaves, ver. 1-14. II. Christ's walking upon the water, ver. 15-21. III. The people's flocking after him to Capernaum, ver. 22-25. IV. His conference with them, occasioned by the miracle of the loaves, in which he reproves them for seeking carnal food, and directs them to spiritual food (ver. 26, 27), showing them how they must labour for spiritual food (ver. 28, 29), and what that spiritual food is, ver. 30-59. V.
6.s: I Am the Bread of Life
6.i: After feeding the crowd, Jesus told them that the bread they really needed was Himself, the bread of life that gives lasting life.
6.p: Lord Jesus, You are the Bread of Life. Feed our hungry hearts and keep us coming to You every day. Amen.
6.l: At your next meal, when you eat bread, take a moment to thank Jesus for being the Bread of Life.
q: The crowd followed Jesus for the free meal. What do you really come to Him for?

7.o: In this chapter we have, I. Christ's declining for some time to appear publicly in Judea, ver. 1. II. His design to go up to Jerusalem at the feast of tabernacles, and his discourse with his kindred in Galilee concerning his going up to this feast, ver. 2-13. III. His preaching publicly in the temple at that feast. 1. In the midst of the feast, ver. 14, 15. We have his discourse with the Jews, (1.) Concerning his doctrine, ver. 16-18. (2.) Concerning the crime of sabbath-breaking laid to his charge, ver. 19-24. (3.
7.i: At the Feast of Tabernacles a priest poured out water from the Pool of Siloam every morning. On the last day Jesus stood up and offered something that never runs out.
7.p: Lord Jesus, You cried out to the thirsty. Fill us with Your Spirit, and let it flow out to others. Amen.
7.l: The next time you pour yourself a glass of water, stop for a second and thank Jesus for the kind of life that never runs dry.
q: A pitcher gets emptied, and a spring keeps flowing. What are you drawing from that keeps running out?

8.o: In this chapter we have, I. Christ's evading the snare which the Jews laid for him, in bringing to him a woman taken in adultery, ver. 1-11. II. Divers discourses or conferences of his with the Jews that cavilled at him, and sought occasion against him, and made every thing he said a matter of controversy. 1. Concerning his being the light of the world, ver. 12-20. 2. Concerning the ruin of the unbelieving Jews, ver. 21-30. 3. Concerning liberty and bondage, ver. 31-37. 4.
8.s: I Am the Light of the World
8.i: John 8 holds three of Jesus' best-known sayings: no stone for the woman, I am the light of the world, and before Abraham was, I am.
8.p: Lord Jesus, light of the world, forgive us as You forgave her. Help us to extend to others the mercy You gave us. Amen.
8.l: When you see someone else get into trouble today, remember Jesus' words and think before you blame.
q: Jesus appealed to two witnesses, himself and the Father. Who are the two or three witnesses to what you believe?

9.o: After Christ's departure out of the temple, in the close of the foregoing chapter, and before this happened which is recorded in this chapter, he had been for some time abroad in the country, it is supposed about two or three months; in which interval of time Dr. Lightfoot and other harmonists place all the passages that occur from Luke x. 17 to xiii. 17. What is recorded in ch. vii. and viii.
9.s: Go, Wash in the Pool of Siloam
9.i: Jesus healed a man blind from birth by putting mud on his eyes and sending him to wash in the pool of Siloam, and later revealed Himself to the man as the Son of Man.
9.p: Lord Jesus, You are the light of the world. Open our eyes to see You, and give us hearts that believe. Amen.
9.l: Look carefully at something small today, a leaf, a face, a color. Thank God for your eyes.
q: The man could not see Jesus, but he obeyed. What has Jesus told you to do that you cannot yet see the reason for?

10.o: In this chapter we have, I. Christ's parabolical discourse concerning himself as the door of the sheepfold, and the shepherd of the sheep, ver. 1-18. II. The various sentiments of people upon it, ver. 19-21. III. The dispute Christ had with the Jews in the temple at the feast of dedication, ver. 22-39. IV. His departure into the country thereupon, ver. 40-42.
10.i: In Jesus' day a family's sheepfold sat inside the outer gate of the house, so only the porter or the master could let anyone in the right way. That is the picture behind a thief who has to climb.
10.l: Learn one thing today about how God speaks to you, and listen for it.
q: Sheep follow the voice they know and run from a stranger's. Whose voice are you following most this week?

11.o: In this chapter we have the history of that illustrious miracle which Christ wrought a little before his death—the raising of Lazarus to life, which is recorded only by this evangelist; for the other three confine themselves to what Christ did in Galilee, where he resided most, and scarcely ever carried their history into Jerusalem till the passion-week: whereas John's memoirs relate chiefly to what passed at Jerusalem; this passage therefore was reserved for his pen.
11.i: Jesus waited two days, wept with Mary and Martha, and then called Lazarus out of a tomb after four days, showing He is the resurrection and the life.
11.p: Lord Jesus, You wept at a grave and You called life out of it. Comfort those who grieve, and give us hope in You. Amen.
11.l: If someone you know is sad, sit with them today. You do not have to fix it, just stay close, the way Jesus did.
q: Jesus cried with Mary and Martha before He raised Lazarus. Whom could you sit with in sadness today?

12.o: It was a melancholy account which we had in the close of the foregoing chapter of the dishonour done to our Lord Jesus, when the scribes and Pharisees proclaimed him a traitor to their church, and put upon him all the marks of ignominy they could: but the story of this chapter balances that, by giving us an account of the honour done to the Redeemer, notwithstanding all that reproach thrown upon him. Thus the one was set over against the other.
12.i: John 12 pictures a dinner in Bethany where one friend's extravagant gift brings out what the people in the room really valued.
12.p: Lord Jesus, You are worth more than all we have. Take our best, and let our lives smell of love for You. Amen.
12.l: Give your best to someone today, a thank-you, your time, or a gift that costs you something.
q: Mary gave her best without counting the cost. What is the best thing you could offer Jesus today?

13.o: Our Saviour having finished his public discourses, in which he "endured the contradiction of sinners," now applies himself to a private conversation with his friends, in which he designed the consolation of saints. Henceforward we have an account of what passed between him and his disciples, who were to be entrusted with the affairs of his household, when he was gone into a far country; the necessary instructions and comforts he furnished them with.
13.s: He loved them to the very end
13.i: Judas came to be trusted because, when the twelve travelled together, someone had to act as steward of the small society, and the job fell to him.
13.l: Be kind today to someone who has let you down.
q: Jesus kept a kindness for His disciples though there was a Judas among them. Who needs your kindness even though they have let you down?

14.o: This chapter is a continuation of Christ's discourse with his disciples after supper. When he had convicted and discarded Judas, he set himself to comfort the rest, who were full of sorrow upon what he had said of leaving them, and a great many good words and comfortable words he here speaks to them. The discourse in interlocutory; as Peter in the foregoing chapter, so Thomas, and Philip, and Jude, in this interposed their thoughts upon what he said, according to the liberty he was pleased to allow them.
14.i: At the Last Supper, Jesus comforts his troubled friends and tells them that he is the way to the Father.
14.p: Lord Jesus, You are the way home. When we are worried, help us to trust You and follow. Amen.
14.l: If someone you know is worried today, tell them gently that Jesus is with them.
q: Jesus said He is the way, not just that He knows the way. What difference does that make?

15.o: It is generally agreed that Christ's discourse in this and the next chapter was at the close of the last supper, the night in which he was betrayed, and it is a continued discourse, not interrupted as that in the foregoing chapter was; and what he chooses to discourse of is very pertinent to the present sad occasion of a farewell sermon. Now that he was about to leave them, I.
15.i: The night before His death, Jesus told His disciples that He is the true vine and they are the branches who can bear fruit only by staying connected to Him.
15.p: Lord Jesus, You are the vine. Keep us connected to You, and make us fruitful in love. Amen.
15.l: Spend a few minutes alone with Jesus today, reading a Bible verse or talking to Him, to stay connected.
q: A branch bears fruit only by staying in the vine. How do you stay close to Jesus on a busy day?

16.o: Among other glorious things God hath spoken of himself this is one, I wound, and I heal, Deut. xxxii. 39. Christ's discourse in this chapter, which continues and concludes his farewell sermon to his disciples, does so. I. Here are wounding words in the notice he gives them of the troubles that were before them, ver. 1-6. II. Here are healing words in the comforts he administers to them for their support under those troubles, which are five:—1. That he would send them the Comforter, ver. 7-15. 2.
16.i: John 16 is part of Jesus' last talk with His friends before the cross: a warning, a promise of the Helper, and a promise of peace.
16.p: Holy Spirit, our Helper, guide us into truth and give us the peace of Jesus when we are afraid. Amen.
16.l: When something feels hard today, say this out loud: Jesus has overcome the world.
q: The Father is with his people even alone. Where do you most need that reminder this week?

17.o: This chapter is a prayer, it is the Lord's prayer, the Lord Christ's prayer. There was one Lord's prayer which he taught us to pray, and did not pray himself, for he needed not to pray for the forgiveness of sin; but this was properly and peculiarly his, and suited him only as a Mediator, and is a sample of his intercession, and yet is of use to us both for instruction and encouragement in prayer. Observe, I. The circumstances of the prayer, ver. 1. II. The prayer itself. 1. He prays for himself, ver. 1-5. 2.
17.i: John 17 is Jesus' prayer on the night before the cross, and it is full of His love for people who had not even been born yet.
17.p: Father, thank You that Jesus prayed for us. Make us one in Your love, and keep us safe in Your name. Amen.
17.l: Pray today for someone in your family, and tell them you did.
q: Unity in love is what draws others in. Who could be drawn to your church or family by how you treat the person you disagree with?

18.o: Hitherto this evangelist has recorded little of the history of Christ, only so far as was requisite to introduce his discourses; but now that the time drew nigh that Jesus must die he is very particular in relating the circumstances of his sufferings, and some which the others had omitted, especially his sayings. So far were his followers from being ashamed of his cross, or endeavouring to conceal it, that this was what, both by word and writing, they were most industrious to proclaim, and gloried in it.
18.s: The Garden, the Fire, and the Question
18.i: John 18 tells of an arrest in a garden, a denial around a fire, and a king who stands before a governor.
18.p: Lord Jesus, You walked into the garden knowing what was coming. Give us courage to say we are Yours. Amen.
18.l: If someone asks whether you follow Jesus today, practice saying yes out loud.
q: Annas lost his office but kept his influence. Who in your life holds power without holding the title?

19.o: Though in the history hitherto this evangelist seems industriously to have declined the recording of such passages as had been related by the other evangelists, yet, when he comes to the sufferings and death of Christ, instead of passing them over, as one ashamed of his Master's chain and cross, and looking upon them as the blemishes of his story, he repeats what had been before related, with considerable enlargements, as one that desired to know nothing but Christ and him crucified, to glory in nothing save in…
19.i: In John 19, in the middle of the crucifixion, Jesus stops to take care of His mother and then declares His work finished.
19.p: Lord Jesus, You finished the work the Father gave You, and You cared for those You loved. Thank You. Amen.
19.l: Do something today to take care of someone in your family, the way Jesus took care of His mother.
q: Even in agony, Jesus cared for His mother. Who in your life do you need to take care of in a practical way?

20.o: This evangelist, though he began not his gospel as the rest did, yet concludes it as they did, with the history of Christ' resurrection; not of the thing itself, for none of them describe how he rose, but of the proofs and evidences of it, which demonstrated that he was risen. The proofs of Christ's resurrection, which we have in this chapter, are I. Such as occurred immediately at the sepulchre. 1. The sepulchre found empty, and the graveclothes in good order, ver. 1-10. 2.
20.i: Mary Magdalene found the tomb empty and met the risen Jesus, who called her by name and sent her to tell the others.
20.p: Risen Lord Jesus, You call each of us by name. Open our eyes to see You, and send us to tell others. Amen.
20.l: Tell someone good news today, as Mary did: a joy you have, shared out loud.
q: Mary knew Jesus when He said her name. How would you answer if He spoke yours?

21.o: The evangelist seemed to have concluded his history with the foregoing chapter; but (as St. Paul sometimes in his epistles), new matter occurring, he begins again. He had said that there were many other signs which Jesus did for the proof of his resurrection. And in this chapter he mentions one of these many, which was Christ's appearance to some of his disciples at the sea of Tiberias, in which we have an account, I.
21.i: The risen Jesus filled his friends' empty nets at dawn, cooked them breakfast on the shore, and three times invited Peter to feed His sheep.
21.p: Lord Jesus, You cooked breakfast for failed fishermen and gave a fresh start to a failed friend. Restore us and send us out. Amen.
21.l: Think of someone you let down. Today, tell them you are sorry, or do something kind to show it.
q: Jesus answered Peter's three denials with three invitations. Where do you need a fresh start with Him?
